newsitem.title: CHINA: China disappointed at rights censure move in U.N.
newsitem.headline: China disappointed at rights censure move in U.N.

text.p: China's Foreign Ministry voiced disappointment on Friday at a move by the United States and Denmark to table a joint resolution criticising China's human rights record in the United Nations.
Ties with Denmark would be damaged by the move, Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said.
"They have deliberately resorted to confrontation by co-sponsoring the motion and we feel great regret at their move," Shen said.
"We believe the decicsion taken by Denmark will cause damage to the bilateral relations between China and Denmark," Shen said.
China had made great strides in protecting the human rights of its people and would do more, he said.

In Geneva, diplomatic sources said support for the Western-backed motion seemed to be eroding, making it increasingly likely that Beijing will escape censure again for the seventh straight year when the 53-member forum votes next Tuesday.
